# Basics

## **Core Concept**

* **Genre:** 2D side-view, fast-paced micro-management roguelike.  
* **Core Loop:** Gather resources, breed workers, attack enemies, defend the nest, survive and upgrade..  
* **The Goal of run:** Survive exactly one year across multiple seasons until winter, creating as many new queens and mates as possible before your run ends.

## **Introduction**

You as a player are a Wasp queen, and your duty is to manage, defend and spread. You have to take care of your nest, breed other wasps, which are going to help you. You have to gather food and resources to expand your nest and defend it from predators. But be careful, your wasps aren’t that loyal and could anytime betray you.

## **Controls**

* **The Queen:** The player's mouse acts as the Queen wasp, performing all actions physically.  
* **No Menus or Storage:** There are no storage warehouses or resource quantity bars; every action requires a physical response.  
* **Physical Management:** You must drag cardboard to the nest to build hexagonal cells, click on cells to lay an egg, drag food directly to hungry larvae, and click on incoming enemies to sting them.  
  Also drag and punish traitor wasps, and eat their eggs by spotting them and clicking them.

## **Wasps workers**

* **Autonomous Workers:** Hatched wasps act on priorities without player control: building, feeding larvae, and defending against threats.  
* **Rebellions & Impostors:** Workers may secretly lay rebel eggs in empty cells or act against the Queen.  
* **Punishing Mutiny:** Traitors are identified by evasive movements, suspicion actions or heavy resistance when grabbed, and must be physically thrown or shaken with the mouse to submit. Then they are injured and weakened. 

## **Layout**

* **Environment Design:** The top screen features a left cardboard source, a central enemy spawn, and a right food source ("restaurant").  
* **Nest Layout:** The bottom screen houses the central Hexagonal Nest, Info panel (left), and Upgrades panel (right).  
* **(Additional) Roguelike Upgrades:** Generating queens and mates before winter yields Meta-progression points to spend on permanent upgrades in subsequent runs.

# Details

## **Core Gameplay**

* **Perspective & Controls:** 2D side-view where the mouse is the Queen, utilizing physical drag-and-drop or click actions.  
    
* **UI Philosophy:** Zero storage bars or menus; resources exist only in the environment or in a worker's mandibles.  
    
* **Game Loop:** Gather \> Build Cells \> Lay Eggs \> Feed Larvae \> Defend \> Winter Death (Roguelike Reset). And always keep an eye on the other workers.  
     
* **Seasons:** There would be 4 seasons, and in each one your goal is different.


## **Resource Management**

* **Gathering:** Drag cardboard from the top-left to build cells; drag food from the top-right directly to larvae.  
    
* **Overproduction:** When a player gathers too much food, or wasp is carrying the food to the destination and the player fills up the destination, she could change the destination to other larvae or drop it to the ground and it will rot.

## **Life Cycle**

To maintain the fast-paced chaos, the Queen and autonomous workers follow a strict biological cycle.

| Life Phase | Duration | Food Needed | Outcome & Mechanics |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Egg** | 30 seconds | None | You have to hold in an empty cell for 5 seconds to lay it. |
| **Larva** |  3 minutes | 9 units | Hunger every minute. Then you have 20 seconds to feed it with 3 units of food. Dies and rots if left unfed. |
| **Pupa** | 1 minute | None | The cell is capped shut. If disrupted, dies. |
| **Adult** | Until dead | [Feeds from larvae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paper_wasp#:~:text=Paper%20wasps%20feed%20on%20sugars%20like%20nectar%2C%20aphid%20honeydew%20and%20the%20sugary%20liquid%20produced%20by%20their%20larvae.) | Works for the queen, can rebel or can die when defending the nest. Or could be killed by you.  |

## **Wasp behavior**

1. **Wasp Priority 1 (Defend):** If enemies are present, drop all resources and attack immediately.  
     
2. **Wasp Priority 2 (Feed):** If larvae are actively hungry, fetch food from the restaurant.  
     
3. **Wasp Priority 3 (Build):** If no empty cells exist, fetch cardboard.  
     
4. **Wasp Priority 4 (Clean):** Remove dead wasps or rotting resources to prevent disease.  
   

## **Traitors**

* **The Traitor System:** Each wasp has a hidden bar of rebellion. It automatically fills up and when it is full, the wasp becomes a traitor. She has a chance to lay rebel eggs in empty cells or to start attacking others or to destroy the nest or kill Pupa.   
    
* **Subduing Mutiny:** Traitors show heavy physical drag resistance and must be thrown against walls or shaken by the Queen to force them into obedient labor.  
     
* **Born Traitor**: If you let the traitor eggs hatch, they are going to be born into full traitors, their rebellion bar is going to be always full and you have to kill them.


## **Player interaction**

* Can drag resources from resource piles, on the left it is cardboard for building the nest and on the right is food for feeding the larvae  
* Can drag only one thing and one unit of something  
    
* Can drag wasps around, throw them or shake with them  
* Can drag cardboard to the nest grid to build empty cells  
* Can lay the eggs by holding for 5 seconds in the build cell.  
* Can feed larvae by dragging the food  
* Can click on the enemies to sting them and scare them away  
* Can hold for 5 seconds on the egg to eat it


## **Meta-progression**

* **Endgame (Winter):** Produce Royals (Queens/Mates) in late Autumn to earn Meta-Points for permanent run upgrades.

## **Info**

Orange items are additional, and probably won’t be in the game for game jam
